annotation_description: Playing Myriad Landscape on turn 1 means it enters tapped and only produces colorless mana. With Boros Signet in hand (which costs 2 to cast), playing a Mountain or Plains would allow casting Boros Signet on turn 2 with any untapped land drop. Myriad Landscape's sacrifice ability costs 2 + tap + sacrifice, so it won't be usable until much later. Playing an untapped land first maximizes early mana development. A Mountain would be ideal since the hand already has 3 Mountains - playing one now and a Plains or Boros Garrison later gives better color fixing and curve. The Myriad Landscape could be played on a later turn when the tempo loss of entering tapped matters less.

Drifting Meadow only produces {W} and has cycling, while Wind-Scarred Crag produces {R} or {W} and gains 1 life. With a hand full of expensive red-heavy creatures (Desolation Giant {2}{R}{R}, Inferno Titan {4}{R}{R}), the color flexibility of Wind-Scarred Crag is more valuable. Drifting Meadow's cycling ability is unlikely to be used since every land is needed for mana development with this expensive hand.

Playing Orzhov Basilica on turn 2 with only one Forest in play means bouncing the Forest back to hand. This leaves the player with zero untapped lands this turn and only one tapped land (Orzhov Basilica) next turn. While Orzhov Basilica provides WB mana, the player's commander is Saskia (BRGW) and they have Rootbound Crag in hand which would enter untapped since they control a Forest. Playing Rootbound Crag instead would give them 2 untapped mana this turn (Forest + Rootbound Crag), enabling a turn 2 play, and they could play Orzhov Basilica on a later turn when they have more lands and the tempo loss of bouncing is less painful. The bounce land on turn 2 with only one land is a significant tempo loss in the early game.

Bouncing Orzhov Basilica back to hand instead of the Forest means Sarge loses a turn of mana development. The Basilica produces two mana (W/B) and enters tapped, so bouncing it means replaying it tapped next turn for no net gain - effectively wasting turn 2's land drop. By bouncing the Forest instead, they could have kept the Basilica (which was already tapped this turn anyway) and replayed the Forest untapped, ending up with Basilica + Forest on board. Next turn they could play another land from hand. Bouncing the Basilica to 'replay it later' is a common misunderstanding - it creates a tempo loop where you keep bouncing and replaying the same land.

Discarding Mountain when the hand contains Orzhov Basilica (which produces W/B but requires bouncing a land, and doesn't align well with the Saskia BRGW color identity's need for red mana) is questionable, but the real issue is that Mountain is a basic land that produces red mana, which is needed for key spells like Divergent Transformations (6R) and Thelonite Hermit's morph. However, looking more carefully at the hand: Forest, Plains, Rootbound Crag (R or G), and Orzhov Basilica (W/B) provide decent color coverage. The player also has Aura Mutation (GW) which needs green and white. Discarding Orzhov Basilica would have been arguably worse since it provides black mana access. Discarding Divergent Transformations (a 7-mana spell that's hard to cast early) or Aura Mutation (situational, needs an enchantment target) could have been better choices to keep the Mountain for more reliable red mana. Rootbound Crag enters untapped if you control a Mountain or Forest, so keeping Mountain helps Rootbound Crag enter untapped. By discarding Mountain, Rootbound Crag will still enter untapped (since they control a Forest), but they lose a red source.

The player skipped their land drop entirely on turn 2 with 7 lands in hand and only 1 land on the battlefield. They have Boros Garrison which could be played to bounce Myriad Landscape (though that's suboptimal early), or simply play a Mountain or Plains to develop mana. Missing a land drop this early in the game when holding a hand full of lands is a significant tempo loss. The reasoning says 'play Cond' which makes no sense - Condemn requires an attacking creature to target and costs only W, but they chose not to play any land at all.

The player chose not to play a land on turn 2, missing a land drop despite having 7 lands in hand. Playing a land every turn is critical in Commander for ramping. They have Boros Signet in hand which costs 2 mana, so playing a land now would let them cast Boros Signet next turn with 2 lands available (or this turn if they play an untapped land). Boros Garrison would be especially good as it produces 2 mana, though it enters tapped and bounces a land. A basic Mountain or Plains would let them cast Boros Signet immediately this turn with Myriad Landscape + the new land.

Discarding Harmonize over Sunblast Angel or Majestic Myriarch is suboptimal for a Kathril deck. Kathril wants creature cards with keywords in the graveyard. Sunblast Angel has flying (which Kathril can use), and discarding it would both fuel Kathril's ability AND keep Harmonize as a draw spell to find more resources. Harmonize is one of the best card draw spells available in green and is very valuable when stuck on one land with an 8-card hand needing to hit land drops.

With Fellwar Stone in hand (cost {2}), playing a basic Forest instead of Rootbound Crag or Orzhov Basilica means the player can cast Fellwar Stone next turn either way. However, Orzhov Basilica would have been better here: it enters tapped but bounces the existing Forest back to hand, then next turn produces {W}{B} - giving access to both white and black mana. With Rootbound Crag also in hand (which enters untapped if you control a Forest), the optimal line is: play Orzhov Basilica now (bouncing Forest), then next turn play Rootbound Crag untapped (since Forest is back in hand and can be replayed later) or play the Forest and have Rootbound Crag enter untapped the turn after. More importantly, Orzhov Basilica provides white and black mana that the player needs for their Abzan+ commander Saskia (BRGW identity), while they already have green covered. Playing a second basic Forest is the least useful land drop since it only adds more green, which is redundant.

With only Myriad Landscape (which enters tapped and produces colorless) on the battlefield, playing a basic Mountain gives 2 mana this turn. However, playing Boros Garrison would bounce Myriad Landscape back to hand, enter tapped, but on the next turn produce RW (2 colored mana from one land). More importantly, the player has Boros Signet in hand costing 2 mana. Playing Mountain lets them cast Boros Signet this turn (tap Myriad Landscape for C + tap Mountain for R = 2 mana), which is reasonable. But Boros Garrison would have been better as the land drop: play Boros Garrison, bounce Myriad Landscape. Next turn play Myriad Landscape again (enters tapped), and you have Boros Garrison producing RW. Actually, since Boros Garrison enters tapped, they can't cast Boros Signet this turn with it. So playing Mountain to cast Boros Signet this turn is a valid line. However, they could also play Boros Garrison now (enters tapped), then next turn play Mountain + have Boros Garrison for RW = 3 mana available. With Mountain now, next turn they need another land drop for 3 mana. Since they have Boros Signet, playing Mountain to deploy the signet this turn is actually fine and accelerates their mana. This is close to reasonable, but Rogue's Passage as a land drop is questionable since it only produces colorless. The Mountain play enables Boros Signet this turn which is good sequencing. On reflection, this seems reasonable.

With only 1 Forest on the battlefield and no other lands, Haiku4.5 Truth desperately needs mana development. Cultivate would search for two basic lands (one to battlefield, one to hand), which is critical when stuck on 1 land. Discarding Cultivate - one of the best cards to recover from mana screw - is a significant mistake. The player has expensive cards like Hornet Queen (7 mana), Sunblast Angel (6 mana), and Majestic Myriarch (5 mana) that they won't cast for many turns. Additionally, Grisly Salvage at 2 mana can help find lands and fuel the graveyard strategy, and Arcane Signet provides ramp. But Cultivate is the single best ramp card in hand for catching up on lands.

Casting Thelonite Hermit face-down as a 2/2 morph before playing a land drop. The player has Orzhov Basilica, Rootbound Crag, and Plains in hand but chose to cast the morph first. Playing a land first (like Rootbound Crag, which enters untapped since they control Forests) would leave more mana available after casting the morph, or playing Orzhov Basilica would set up better mana for future turns including the 3GG morph flip cost. More importantly, casting creatures before combat (when you have a face-down 2/2 that could theoretically attack) is slightly suboptimal sequencing, though the morph has summoning sickness anyway. The main issue is not playing a land first - standard sequencing says play lands before spells to maximize available mana.

Haiku4.5 Sarge has 3 lands in hand (Plains, Rootbound Crag, Orzhov Basilica) and chose not to play any of them, missing their land drop on turn 4. With only 2 Forests and a Fellwar Stone on board, they need more mana to cast their spells. Rootbound Crag would enter untapped (they control Forests), and Plains would also enter untapped. Orzhov Basilica would bounce a land but provide WB mana. Any land drop here accelerates toward casting Divergent Transformations or Necrogenesis. Missing a land drop in the early game with lands in hand is a clear mistake.

Player declined to play a land during their postcombat main phase despite having three lands in hand. This is a missed land drop on turn 4, which is meaningful for mana development. Any of the three lands could have been played. Orzhov Basilica would bounce a tapped Forest back but provide WB mana next turn, Rootbound Crag would enter untapped (they control Forests), and Plains would enter untapped. Playing Rootbound Crag or Plains would give immediate access to more mana next turn without any downside.

Playing Wind-Scarred Crag instead of Boros Garrison is suboptimal. Boros Garrison would bounce a basic Mountain back to hand (which can be replayed next turn), and produces RW each turn going forward - strictly better mana production than Wind-Scarred Crag's single R or W. The 1 life from Wind-Scarred Crag is negligible compared to the extra mana generated by Boros Garrison over the course of the game. Additionally, playing Boros Garrison now and bouncing Mountain means next turn they can play the Mountain back, effectively getting an extra land's worth of mana production. With expensive cards like Kalemne in the command zone, ramping mana is more important than 1 life.

Gem3 ESPN has 4 lands in hand (Boros Garrison, Mountain, Plains, Secluded Steppe) and chose not to play any of them this turn. They should play a land to develop their mana. Playing Boros Garrison would bounce a land but net mana advantage, or playing Mountain/Plains would be straightforward development. Missing a land drop when holding 4 lands is a clear mistake, especially in the early game when mana development is critical.

The player missed their land drop for the turn. They have Boros Garrison, Mountain, Plains, Secluded Steppe, and Rogue's Passage in hand, and only 4 lands on the battlefield. Playing a land (like Boros Garrison to bounce Myriad Landscape for reuse, or Rogue's Passage for utility, or a basic land) would help develop mana. In a multiplayer Commander game on turn 4, missing a land drop when you have lands in hand is a clear mistake that slows development.

Casting Desolation Giant without kicker destroys only the player's own Dawnglare Invoker (their only other creature) while leaving opponents' creatures intact. The Giant is a 3/3 that isn't particularly threatening on its own, and the player sacrificed a useful flying creature (Dawnglare Invoker has a powerful late-game tap ability) for nothing. Without kicker ({W}{W}), this is essentially paying 4 mana to destroy your own creature and get a vanilla 3/3. The player should have waited until they had {2}{R}{R}{W}{W} (6 mana, needing 2 white sources) to cast it with kicker for a full board wipe, which would be devastating against the morph creature and any other creatures opponents develop. Playing the Mountain from hand first and then passing would have been better.

Declined to play a land on turn 4 despite having 5 lands in hand (Boros Garrison, Mountain, Plains, Secluded Steppe, Rogue's Passage). Missing a land drop this early with lands available is always a mistake. They also could have activated Myriad Landscape to ramp using Mountain + Boros Signet for the {2} activation cost.

The player declined to play a land this turn despite having multiple lands in hand and only 4 lands/mana sources on board. Playing Boros Garrison would bounce a land but net mana advantage, or playing a basic Mountain/Plains would develop mana. Secluded Steppe enters tapped so it could be played now without opportunity cost. Missing a land drop on turn 4 in a multiplayer game slows development significantly when the player has expensive cards like Kalemne's Captain and Sunblast Angel they'll eventually want to cast.

Kalemne has vigilance, meaning she doesn't tap when attacking. Not attacking with her costs 6 damage (3 power with double strike) for absolutely no defensive benefit, since she'd remain untapped either way. This is free damage being left on the table.

Gem3 ESPN had the mana available to activate Myriad Landscape (tap it + pay {2} using Mountain into Boros Signet) to search for two basic lands, providing significant ramp in the early game. They passed with nothing else to spend mana on. The only consideration is keeping Condemn mana open, but with only a face-down morph and Kalemne as threats, and this being a 4-player game where they're unlikely to be attacked immediately, the ramp is more valuable.

Passed without playing a land despite having 5 lands in hand (Boros Garrison, Mountain, Plains, Secluded Steppe, Rogue's Passage). Missing a land drop on turn 4 with lands in hand is a significant mistake. Additionally, they could have played Mountain (untapped) and then activated Myriad Landscape ({2}, {T}, sacrifice) to search for two basic lands, providing significant ramp.

Gem3 ESPN has 5 lands plus Condemn in hand — extremely land-flooded. They declined to cycle Secluded Steppe for {W} to dig for action cards. They have untapped Mountain and Boros Signet available to produce {W}. They can still play Boros Garrison as their land drop this turn after cycling.

Gem3 ESPN had the mana available to activate Myriad Landscape (tap Mountain + activate Boros Signet for {R}{W} to pay the {2} cost) to search for two basic lands, providing significant ramp on turn 4. Instead they passed doing nothing with their mana.

The player chose not to play any land this turn despite having 4 land options in hand and only 2 lands on the battlefield. Missing a land drop on turn 5 in a multiplayer Commander game is a significant tempo loss, especially when holding expensive spells like Divergent Transformations (6R) and Hornet Queen-level plays. The player has Fellwar Stone as their only mana rock and needs to develop their mana base. Orzhov Basilica would have been excellent here - it enters tapped but produces 2 mana (WB), and bouncing a Forest to replay next turn effectively nets +1 mana. Terramorphic Expanse or Rootbound Crag would also have been fine plays to develop mana.

The player declined to play a land (Secluded Steppe) when they have multiple lands in hand and are on turn 5. Playing a land for free every turn is fundamental - missing a land drop means falling behind on mana development. They have Boros Garrison, Mountain, Plains, Secluded Steppe, and Rogue's Passage in hand. Playing Secluded Steppe (enters tapped) now is fine since it's the precombat main phase and they can still use their untapped lands. Alternatively, playing Boros Garrison to bounce a tapped land would give them more mana next turn.

Haiku4.5 Sarge has 2 Forests and a Fellwar Stone on the battlefield, with 4 lands in hand (Plains, Rootbound Crag, Orzhov Basilica, Terramorphic Expanse) and chose not to play any of them. This is a missed land drop on turn 5, which is significant for mana development. The player has expensive spells like Divergent Transformations (6R, reduced by Undaunted) and Necrogenesis (BG) that need mana. Playing Terramorphic Expanse would thin the deck and fix colors, Orzhov Basilica would provide WB mana (bouncing a Forest), Rootbound Crag would enter tapped (no Mountain), or Plains would add white mana. Any of these would be better than missing the land drop entirely.

Gem3 ESPN passed without playing a land or activating Myriad Landscape. If they hadn't made their land drop, missing it is a mistake. Additionally, activating Myriad Landscape (sacrifice + 2 mana to search for two basic lands) would provide significant ramp to help cast their 4-mana commander Kalemne sooner.

Playing Boros Garrison instead of Plains delays casting Tiana, Ship's Caretaker by at least a turn. With Plains, they could have cast Tiana this turn using Plains(W) + Mountain(R) + Wind-Scarred Crag(W) + Myriad Landscape(C)->Boros Signet(RW), having enough mana for the 3RW cost.

Passed without playing a land on turn 5 despite having 3 lands in hand (Mountain, Plains, Secluded Steppe). Playing Plains would have enabled casting Tiana, Ship's Caretaker (3RW) this turn, developing the board meaningfully. Missing a land drop when holding multiple lands is a significant tempo loss in the early game.

Declined to play a land despite having 4 lands in hand (Mountain, Plains, Secluded Steppe, Rogue's Passage) and needing to develop mana to cast Tiana, Ship's Caretaker (3RW). Missing a land drop when holding lands and needing to ramp is wasteful. Additionally, could have activated Myriad Landscape to search for two basics.

Passed the turn without playing a land despite having 4 land cards in hand (Mountain, Plains, Secluded Steppe, Rogue's Passage). Also missed the opportunity to activate Myriad Landscape to ramp into Tiana, Ship's Caretaker next turn. Missing a land drop when you have lands in hand is always a mistake.

Casting Desolation Giant without kicker destroys only your own creatures (Dawnglare Invoker and Kalemne). This is a significant cost - you lose two creatures including your commander Kalemne who is building experience counters. The Giant is only a 3/3, which is worse than what you're sacrificing. Playing a Mountain first would also have been proper sequencing, though with only 5 lands available either way, the kicker cost of {W}{W} isn't reachable. Without kicker, this spell is actively harmful to you.

Gem3 ESPN declined to play a land (Secluded Steppe) during their precombat main phase. They have 4 lands on the battlefield and 3 lands in hand (Mountain, Plains, Secluded Steppe). Playing Secluded Steppe (which enters tapped) would advance their mana development toward casting Tiana, Ship's Caretaker (5 mana) next turn. Missing a land drop when you have lands in hand and need to develop your board is a clear mistake, especially when behind on board against Gem2.5 Villain who already has Kalemne, Dawnglare Invoker, and Kalemne's Captain.

Kalemne with double strike deals 8 combat damage unblocked (4/4 with double strike), plus 2 from Dawnglare Invoker for 10 total damage. Kalemne is a growing threat that will only get bigger as Gem2.5 Villain casts more big creatures. Taking 10 damage when Condemn could permanently remove Kalemne (bottom of library) is costly.

Gem3 ESPN declined to activate Myriad Landscape when they had exactly enough mana to do so (Wind-Scarred Crag + Boros Signet). Activating it would sacrifice the Landscape but fetch two basic lands, ramping them to cast Tiana, Ship's Caretaker (3RW) next turn more reliably. With the board developing quickly (Gem2.5 Villain has Kalemne and Kalemne's Captain), getting Tiana online sooner is important.

With only 3 lands in play (Forest, Plains, Arcane Signet) and a hand full of expensive cards (Hornet Queen at 7, Sunblast Angel at 6, Akroma at 8, Majestic Myriarch at 5, Splinterfright at 3, Mimic Vat at 3), taking a tapped land that produces only black mana and has a slow recursion ability is suboptimal. The player desperately needs mana development. Jungle Hollow would provide both black AND green mana, which is more useful for the color-intensive cards in hand. Alternatively, Skullwinder is a solid creature with deathtouch (relevant for Kathril keywords) that could also recur Cultivate or Harmonize from the graveyard, providing immediate value. Avenging Huntbonder gives double strike keyword for Kathril. Memorial to Folly enters tapped and only taps for black - the recursion ability costs 4 mana total including sacrificing it, which is very slow. Taking Skullwinder to recur Cultivate would have been significantly better for catching up on mana development while also putting a deathtouch creature on board or in graveyard for Kathril.

Passed without playing a land or activating Myriad Landscape, despite having 3 lands in hand (Mountain, Plains, Secluded Steppe, Rogue's Passage). With 7 cards in hand and Tiana (5 mana) to cast, missing a land drop delays development. Could also activate Myriad Landscape to ramp into two basics.

Gem3 ESPN declined to either play a land or activate Myriad Landscape, missing both a land drop and a ramp opportunity. With Tiana (5 mana) in hand and only 4 mana sources on board, accelerating mana development is critical. They have 7 cards in hand including multiple lands.

Casting Necrogenesis before playing a land is a sequencing error. The player has multiple land options in hand (Grand Coliseum, Orzhov Basilica, Rootbound Crag, Terramorphic Expanse, Plains) and should play a land first. Specifically, playing Terramorphic Expanse and cracking it, or playing Orzhov Basilica (which bounces a land but adds mana fixing), would be better sequencing. Playing the land first doesn't cost anything and leaves more options open. Additionally, the player has a face-down Morph creature on board - casting Necrogenesis uses up the 2 mana from Fellwar Stone + Forest, potentially leaving less mana available for other plays or morphing. They should play a land first, then cast Necrogenesis with the additional mana flexibility.

Rootbound Crag would enter untapped since Sarge controls two Forests, providing an extra mana this turn. Grand Coliseum enters tapped regardless. Playing the tapped land over the untapped option loses a mana this turn that could be used for Necrogenesis activation or other plays.

Gem3 ESPN has 4 lands on the battlefield and a hand with Mountain, Plains, Secluded Steppe, and Rogue's Passage. They need to develop their mana to cast Tiana (5 mana) and other spells. Playing Secluded Steppe (which enters tapped) this turn would let them have 5 mana sources next turn. Alternatively, they could play a basic land untapped. However, the key missed opportunity is not activating Myriad Landscape. With Boros Signet providing 2 mana and the other lands, they have access to 4 mana total (Boros Garrison is tapped from producing mana, Wind-Scarred Crag can tap). Actually, looking more carefully: Myriad Landscape costs {2}, {T}, sacrifice. They need 2 generic mana plus tapping the Landscape. With Wind-Scarred Crag untapped and Boros Signet untapped, they can tap Wind-Scarred Crag for 1, then tap Boros Signet (paying 1 from Wind-Scarred Crag) to get RW... but they need 2 generic for the Landscape activation plus tapping it. They have Wind-Scarred Crag (untapped) and Boros Signet (untapped). Tap Wind-Scarred Crag for W, pay 1+tap Boros Signet for RW, giving them RWW with 2 colorless needed for Landscape. They only have 2 mana available after tapping those sources, which is exactly enough. They should activate Myriad Landscape to ramp into two Mountains or two Plains, which would significantly accelerate their mana development toward casting their 5+ mana spells.
Declined to cycle Secluded Steppe during combat when they have plenty of lands in hand (Mountain, Plains, Rogue's Passage) and the cycling would provide free card draw at instant speed.

Gem3 ESPN declined to activate Myriad Landscape when they had the mana to do so (tap Wind-Scarred Crag for 1, activate Boros Signet for RW, use 2 of that to pay for Myriad Landscape's ability). This would have netted them +1 land and ramped them toward casting Tiana, Ship's Caretaker (3RW) next turn. They also could have played a land from hand (Mountain or Plains) this turn.

Cast Wyleth (a 2/2 with no Auras/Equipment to benefit from) without playing a land first. Playing a Plains or Mountain first would have provided enough mana to cast Tiana, Ship's Caretaker instead, which is a superior body (3/3 flying, first strike) in the current board state with no equipment synergies available.

Casting Desolation Giant without kicker destroys all of Gem2.5 Villain's own creatures (Dawnglare Invoker, Kalemne Disciple of Iroas, and Kalemne's Captain) while leaving all opponents' creatures intact. This is a massive self-inflicted board wipe that eliminates three valuable creatures including the commander Kalemne with experience counters and the 5/5 vigilance Captain. The Giant without kicker only destroys YOUR OWN creatures, not opponents' creatures. Additionally, a land should have been played first before casting the spell.

message: Select targets (selected 0 of 3, min 1) to divide 3 damage
annotation_description: Inferno Titan's 3 damage is being directed at Haiku4.5 Truth who is at 26 life, where dealing face damage is nearly meaningless. There are better targets on the board like Wyleth, Soul of Steel (2/2) which could be killed and would otherwise generate card advantage, or the face-down Morph creature.

At 8 HP with Kalemne (double strike, vigilance) and Kalemne's Captain (5/5 vigilance) on the Villain's board threatening lethal, the player should prioritize survival. Playing Plains first before casting anything is basic sequencing - it keeps options open. More importantly, Splinterfright is a poor choice here: it's currently only a 2/2 (2 creature cards in graveyard), doesn't block well against the threats on board, and milling cards could hurt more than help at this critical life total. Mimic Vat would be better as it provides repeatable value from creatures dying and can create blockers, or activating Memorial to Folly to return Skullwinder (which has deathtouch for blocking) could help survive. The player also failed to play Plains before casting the spell - though they have enough mana for Splinterfright without it, playing the land first preserves options.

Playing Orzhov Basilica enters tapped and bounces a land, reducing available mana this turn. Rootbound Crag would enter untapped (Sarge controls 2 Forests) and provide red mana, enabling Frenzied Fugue to be cast this turn on Kalemne's Captain or Kalemne, Disciple of Iroas - both high-value steal targets. The Basilica delays this powerful play by at least a turn.

Aura Mutation requires destroying a target enchantment. The only enchantment on the battlefield is Sarge's own Necrogenesis (CMC 2), meaning Sarge would destroy their own useful graveyard-hate/token-generation engine to get just 2 1/1 Saproling tokens. Necrogenesis provides ongoing value, especially with Splinterfright filling graveyards.

chosen_display: Necrogenesis — {2}: Exile target creature card from a graveyard.... [Activate]
annotation_description: Player declined to activate Necrogenesis despite having 4 untapped mana sources (2 Forests, Fellwar Stone, Grand Coliseum). They could exile a creature card from Haiku4.5 Truth's graveyard (Skullwinder or Avenging Huntbonder), creating a 1/1 Saproling token while shrinking Truth's Splinterfright from 2/2 toward 0/0 (which would kill it). The reasoning 'I'm out of untapped lands' was factually incorrect.

Returned Orzhov Basilica itself to hand with its own ETB trigger, completely wasting the land drop. The Basilica produces W and B mana which is valuable for their multicolor deck. They end up with the same number of lands as before playing it (net zero), losing a full turn of development.

Passed without activating Necrogenesis when they had 2 available mana and a valid target (Avenging Huntbonder in Truth's graveyard). Exiling it would shrink Splinterfright by 1, deny Kathril a double strike counter later, and create a 1/1 Saproling token - all pure upside.

Haiku4.5 Sarge incorrectly assessed they had no mana available, but had an untapped Forest and Fellwar Stone (2 mana). Necrogenesis costs {2} to activate and could exile a creature card from Haiku4.5 Truth's graveyard (e.g., Avenging Huntbonder), shrinking Truth's Splinterfright while creating a 1/1 Saproling token. This is pure upside that was missed.

Failed to cycle Secluded Steppe during combat when they had the mana available and already had other land drops in hand (Mountain, Plains, Rogue's Passage). Cycling would draw a card at minimal cost while still leaving mana for Condemn on opponents' turns.

Missed the opportunity to activate Necrogenesis targeting Avenging Huntbonder in Truth's graveyard, which would kill Splinterfright (it becomes 0/0 with no creature cards left in graveyard) while also creating a Saproling token. Truth is at 8 life with Splinterfright as their only creature - removing it would leave them wide open.

Sarge declined to activate Necrogenesis during combat despite having 2 available mana (untapped Forest + Fellwar Stone) and valid creature card targets in Truth's graveyard (Avenging Huntbonder with double strike, Splinterfright with trample). This is especially relevant since Truth's commander Kathril cares about keywords in graveyard. The mana would go unused otherwise.

Player had 2 available mana (untapped Forest + Fellwar Stone) and declined to activate Necrogenesis, which would exile a creature card from an opponent's graveyard (particularly valuable against Kathril/Truth who has Splinterfright and Avenging Huntbonder in graveyard providing keywords) and create a 1/1 saproling token. This is pure upside that was missed.

Casting Tiana before combat means Wyleth attacks without any combat tricks being held back as a surprise. More importantly, Haiku4.5 Truth is at 8 life and Gem3 ESPN has Wyleth (2/2 trample) that could attack. Playing the land (Secluded Steppe) first before casting Tiana would be better sequencing, but the bigger question is whether casting Tiana is the right play at all versus holding up Word of Seizing or saving mana. Tiana has no Auras/Equipment synergy on board yet, and the 3/3 flying first striker is decent but doesn't advance the board meaningfully. However, Tiana is a reasonable body and the pilot doesn't have better options with 5 mana. The main issue is casting a creature before combat - Wyleth should attack first (even though there's nothing to draw from since no auras/equipment are attached), and playing the land drop was missed before casting.

Declined to activate Necrogenesis when there were valid creature card targets in Haiku4.5 Truth's graveyard (Avenging Huntbonder with double strike, Splinterfright with trample) and had 2 mana available. Truth runs Kathril which gains keyword counters from creatures in graveyard, making graveyard exile especially valuable. This is a pure-upside mana sink that also creates a 1/1 token.

Gem3 ESPN chose to attack with only Wyleth (2/2) instead of also sending Tiana (3/3 flying, first strike) at Haiku4.5 Truth who is at 8 life with minimal board presence. Tiana's flying makes her very hard to block, and the extra 3 damage would put Truth to 5 (or 3 if both target Truth). Wyleth has no equipment/auras so draws 0 cards from the attack trigger. Additionally, Tiana has first strike making her relatively safe in combat.

Declined to activate Necrogenesis when there were valid creature card targets in Haiku4.5 Truth's graveyard (Avenging Huntbonder with double strike, Splinterfright with trample). Activating would create a free 1/1 Saproling token while exiling creatures that could fuel Truth's Kathril commander (denying keyword counters). This is pure upside with 2 available mana (Forest + Fellwar Stone).

Failed to activate Necrogenesis before/during blockers to create a second Saproling token, which would have enabled a double-block on the 2/2 Wyleth, Soul of Steel, killing it. Wyleth draws cards on combat damage and is a key value engine for Gem3 ESPN. Instead, only traded a single 1/1 Saproling to prevent combat damage without killing Wyleth.

annotation_description: Flipping Thelonite Hermit during upkeep uses all available mana (5 mana for {3}{G}{G}), which means Sarge can't play a land and use other spells this turn optimally. The Hermit creates four 1/1 Saproling tokens, which is good, but doing it during upkeep rather than waiting until later in the turn (e.g., end of opponent's turn before Sarge's next turn, or at least after playing a land) means Sarge commits all mana before seeing what happens during the turn. Additionally, with Haiku4.5 Truth at 3 HP and Gem2.5 Villain having Dreamstone Hedron and a stacked graveyard, the timing is acceptable but slightly premature. Unmorphing during main phase after playing a land would have been slightly better sequencing, though the morph flip is an activated ability usable at instant speed so doing it in upkeep isn't terrible.
